doc.title: Chazz Frichtel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 13, 2016

title: Moving to Nashville and getting the Chuck Mangione call
summary: He moved to Nashville in 1997 and was recommended to Mangione through Grant Geissman and Rick Montalbano, replacing Charles Meeks.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Tell me about Chuck Mangione. Because I got to know him when I was in Rochester as a kid. But that was before he was Chuck Mangione, he was just Chuck Mangione.

Well I started working with Chuck in 2000. And like you, I mean before he broke nationally he was kind of a regional star here with the “Friends and Love” recording. And I loved his music. Never in my wildest dreams did I think that our paths would ever cross all these years later. But I had moved to Nashville in ‘97 because I wanted to check out the songwriting scene and Mike had moved to Nashville and our drummer George Perilli had moved there. And I kind of wanted to take a break from the L.A. treadmill that I was on. And I really wanted to indulge my songwriting. And everybody said it’s a great songwriter’s town, which it is. But I was there and I was still touring with Michael and I

was kind of indulging the songwriting thing, and I got a call from Chuck’s manager, a guy named Richard Burkhart asking me if I was interested. And apparently a guy that I knew in L.A., a bass player named Charles Meeks, who had played with Chuck forever, great Charles, lovely guy, great player, played on all the hits, “Feels So Good” and he decided to retire. And I knew Grant Geissman and I’d played with Grant quite a bit in L.A. He was Chuck’s guitar player, played the famous solo on “Feels So Good.” And so apparently through I think Rick Montalbano recommended me to Chuck. Because they’d been playing together a little bit at The Savoy. And Rick mentioned me to Chuck and then I think Rick said, “Yeah I know this guy, he’s living in Nashville.” And I think Chuck went [sneers] “Nashville.” But then Chuck — as I understand it — called Grant and said, “oh yeah man, I know Chazz, he’d be great for the band.” And next thing I knew I was in New York and we were at SIR playing. And the first couple of gigs I did with Chuck, Ricky was playing, which, Ricky is one of my mentors and dearest friends. So that was a great thrill to be able to connect again.
